meta.title: For agents — give your AI agent a real fly brain
meta.description: Claude skills and tools that run the real 166,700-neuron fruit-fly connectome. fly-mode makes Claude act like a fly whose reactions come from the brain; flyai-compute lets Claude Code run and pay for jobs on fly.ai compute. How to install, integrate and use.

head.title: Give your AI agent a real fly brain
head.lede: Skills and tools that run the MaleCNS v1.0 connectome — all 166,700 neurons of a fruit fly — so an agent can feel, flinch and buzz with a real brain. Open source, runs on your own machine, no token needed.

skills.lede: A Claude skill that turns Claude into a fruit fly. Every reply is driven by what a real fly brain did with your message.
skills.h31: Your message becomes something a fly can feel
skills.p1: A deadline or a swatter looms. Pizza is a taste. "hi cutie" is another fly walking past. Wind, a touch, a smell.
skills.h32: The real connectome runs for one second
skills.p2: Those sense neurons are stimulated in the 166,700-neuron brain, next to the same brain with nothing happening.
skills.h33: Its neurons decide what it does
skills.p3: Escape neurons → jumped. Wing motor neurons → buzzed. Grooming, turning, walking, backing up.
skills.p4: Panic if it jumped, hype if it buzzed, nothing if the brain did nothing — and a brain log line proving it.
skills.h35: What the brain actually did (real runs)
skills.td7: nothing — taste reaches the brain but moves no behaviour neurons
skills.p5: The word-to-sense table is hand-written and is the only made-up part. The reaction is the connectome's — which is why the pizza does nothing, however dramatic the fly wants to be.

install.title: Install in two minutes
install.div1: Install the brainThe first run downloads ~260 MB of brain files.
install.div2: Add the skillCopy the folder from the repo into your skills.
install.div3: Talk to itSay "be a fly". Say "human mode" to stop.
install.p1: The skill is one Python script that prints JSON, so any agent framework, tool call or bot can use it.
install.h32: Or build your own: the flybrain package
install.p2: Everything above runs on flybrain, the whole fly nervous system as a spiking network you can stimulate and read out.

use.title: Talking to the fly
use.li1: It still helps. Ask a real question and the fly answers it, short and distracted.
use.li2: It never fakes a reaction. If the brain did nothing, the fly does nothing. That's the joke, and it's true.
use.li3: Brains are noisy. The same message can land a little differently each time; the script averages three runs.
use.li4: Force a sense with --sense threat|taste|mate|wind|touch|smell when the words don't say it.
use.li5: Runs locally on CPU (or GPU with flybrain[gpu]). Nothing is sent anywhere.

compute.lede: A Claude skill that lets Claude Code run jobs on fly.ai compute. Jobs can be fly-brain experiments, or your own WebAssembly programs and GPU shaders, and they run on browser miners. You say what to run, Claude prices it, and you pay from your own wallet. The results land in a folder.
compute.p1: How many jobs, what each costs, and the most it can cost. Nothing is ordered until you say yes.
compute.h32: You pay with your own wallet
compute.p2: Claude hands you a pay link for $FLYAI. It never asks for or touches a private key.
compute.p3: Browsers around the world run the jobs. You pay for a job only once two miners return the same answer. 80% of each charge goes to them.
compute.p4: One file per job, plus a row saying who checked it. Claude can add jobs to an open order or stop it for you.
compute.p6: Then ask Claude: "run a connectome sweep of looming vs touch on fly.ai compute", or "run my pi.wasm 1,000 times on fly.ai".
